name: Dan Tyminski
notes: The archetype's crossover voice: bluegrass mandolin/guitar and lead vocals in Union Station, and simultaneously the singer on the two records that carried this idiom furthest outside it. The section's own scope note says why this entry looks the way it does: "in this archetype the producer role is largely occupied by instrumental specialists — the players whose parts are the train beat when there is no drum kit, and who also produce records. Each entry below is written as a parameter set for the part they contribute, because that is what the engine needs." The load-bearing parameter here is stated to be the voice — "a high, hard, plain-toned bluegrass lead with almost no vibrato" — so the melody block is the model: a high register, an 0.84 step share, `chordToneBias` 0.86 and `octaveJumpProb` 0.02, which together are as close as this schema gets to a plain-toned lead with almost no vibrato. His place in the stack is stated too — "his vocal sits in the lead (middle) position of the bluegrass stack, with Krauss's tenor above" — hence a countermelody at +12 carrying an octave_echo share rather than a pure answer figure. As a bandleader "his records keep the ensemble train beat but add a kit on the later, rock-leaning material", so the drum block sits between the wings: `kick` [1,3] on anchors 1 and 3, brush-to-stick velocities at 94–112, the hat on quarters, `percs` at −8 dB, `fills` at 8/16. Harmony is the stated G/A/B♭/D with I–IV–V and modal ♭VII, plus a minor i–♭VII–IV family and a natural-minor scale weight because "his solo records ... move progressively toward minor-mode and rock harmony" (the entry lists the three albums the ellipsis drops). ⚠ The BPM band is the acoustic lane only — the entry says the electronic crossover "sits at 4/4 dance tempo and is not modelled here", and it is not modelled here either. `bpm.mode` 110 inside the stated 65–190 is INFERRED. ⚠ Also INFERRED: the velocity tiers, the −4 ms anticipated offset, `percs` contents and every bassline number. ⚠ The entry states "harmonic detail generalised [LOW-CONF]" and rates itself medium-high.
